correctness.rationale: The orthogonal-Grassmannian Schubert basis is indexed by strict partitions with largest part at most n, giving exactly 2^n cells and hence Euler characteristic 2^n. Classical Pieri multiplication by the codimension-one Schubert class adds one box with coefficient one, so the top self-intersection counts standard shifted tableaux of staircase shape. The shifted hook-length formula gives the displayed factorial degree product. The exact adjacent ratio simplifies to a quotient of binomial coefficients; after factoring the increase in the upper binomial parameter, it is exactly two at n=2 and strictly greater than two for every n at least three. The base values at n=4 and n=5 then prove the full strict classification. The bundled checker independently replays the two degree products and all ratio identities.

value.rationale: Spinor varieties are basic minuscule homogeneous varieties, and the two invariants compared here have canonical interpretations: projective degree counts generic complementary linear sections while Euler characteristic counts Schubert cells. The theorem gives a complete all-rank phase diagram with a sharp transition and no equality cases, and the adjacent-ratio identity explains why the transition can occur only once. This is a natural structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
